name: Yirmisekiz Mehmed Çelebi's embassy to Paris
traveler: Yirmisekiz Mehmed Çelebi, ambassador of Ahmed III
summary: The first Ottoman ambassador to stay long in Paris sails to France with eighty attendants, to renew the alliance and, his instructions say, to study what in France is worth learning. Plague in Provence sends him the long way round, by the Canal du Midi and Bordeaux. His Sefâretnâme describes Versailles, the Observatory and the Gobelins, and helped start the Tulip Age's taste for French gardens.

stops.note: He sails on a French ship.
Forty days of quarantine; Marseille is in the grip of the plague.
West by the Canal du Midi, around the plague.
Down the Garonne to the Atlantic side of France.
A grand entry, an audience with the eleven-year-old Louis XV, and five months of gardens, theatres and the Observatory.
Down the Rhône to the sea, and a ship for home.
He gives the grand vizier his account, and French gardens rise on the Bosphorus.

informs.note: France, from the Midi to Versailles
